observations.finding: DMSO f_a63b63b85186: confluent monolayer, flat adherent cells. Blue nuclei ovoid regular, green tubulin as diffuse filamentous network, red F-actin at periphery/ stress fibers. Rare bright rounded cells.

Treated w_246fbe6008 1.0uM f_8d7d1e13d8d7 and f_55e7ca28ae81: markedly sparser adherent layer. 5-10x increase in bright rounded white-yellow cells (overlap of blue DNA + green tubulin + red actin) 10-15 um diameter, most often in doublets/clusters, detached above monolayer. Identical contrast settings so intensity increase is real.

Treated w_2eeef82f69 0.03uM f_24fcc59ce33e and f_50b5b4e93254: same phenotype, intermediate: increased bright rounded mitotic-like cells vs DMSO but fewer clusters than 1.0uM. f_24fcc59ce33e shows central triple bright mitosis and bottom-right large multinucleated/lobed cells; f_50b5b4e93254 shows persistent clusters top-left and bottom-center.
Green tubulin intensity markedly increased in treated cells, especially in and around rounded cells and in interphase cytoplasm, appearing more punctate/textured vs diffuse DMSO network.
Tubulin heterogeneity/texture increased (more contrast, high variation) consistent with condensed mitotic spindles/bundles and loss of diffuse interphase array.
Red F-actin at cortex of rounded cells also brighter and more contrasted; rounded cells show strong cortical actin ring.

Blue DNA signal brighter, more intense white-yellow when overlapped with tubulin/actin in rounded cells, consistent with condensed chromosomes. Integrated DNA amount and mean DNA intensity increased; nuclei larger on average.

Nuclear shape less regular: more lobed, bilobed, indented or fragmented nuclei, decreased solidity and form factor. Visible in large flat cells bottom-center f_8d7d1e13d8d7 and central f_24fcc59ce33e.

notable_cells.why: cluster of bright white-yellow doublet mitotic cells with intense tubulin/DNA overlap vs flat green/red interphase neighbor
central aggregate of ~12 bright rounded cells forming polyploid/mitotic cluster, absent in DMSO

candidate_mechanisms.why: Dominant strong increases in tub_mean z 28.5/17.0, tub_std z 27.3/19.4, tub_glcm_contrast z 40.2/13.4 exclude destabilizers which would decrease tubulin. Mitotic arrest with increased DNA content nuc_dna_integrated z 16.4/19.8 and irregular nuclei.
Also consistent: mitotic arrest, decreased nuc_solidity z -28.3/-19.1, nuc_form_factor z -13.3, increased ploidy, brighter tubulin from mitotic cells.
Also consistent: monopolar mitotic arrest gives same composite appearance; cannot distinguish bipolar vs monopolar without grayscale tubulin/DNA channels.

report.uncertainty: No separate grayscale channels provided; cannot resolve spindle morphology (monopolar rosette vs bipolar/multipolar bundles) to distinguish among Aurora kinase inhibitors, Eg5 inhibitors and Microtubule stabilizers. All are antimitotic; actin/DNA-damage/protein synthesis classes excluded. DNA damage/replication and Actin disruptors ruled out by increased tubulin/actin signals.

data.note:
Correct — AZ-C (BBBC021 internal code, no PubChem structure) is annotated as Eg5 inhibitors and our blinded conclusion Eg5 inhibitors (p=0.64) matched via NSC vote 3/4 and monotonic tubulin enhancement.

Phenotype was antimitotic: marked increase in tub_mean/tub_std/tub_glcm_contrast (z up to +40), increased DNA content, decreased nuclear solidity/form factor, bright rounded mitotic clusters — overlapping with microtubule stabilizers like paclitaxel (taxol/Paclitaxel, Tubulin inhibitor per ChEMBL CHEMBL428647) but resolved toward Eg5 by atlas neighbors to AZ138.

Reflection: Eg5/KIF11 inhibition produces monopolar spindles and mitotic arrest as validated in literature: K858 novel Eg5 inhibitor inducing cancer cell death PMID 19351824, optical control of mitosis with photoswitchable Eg5 inhibitor PMID 34958711, pyrenocine A inducing monopolar spindle formation PMID 31679979; HDAC inhibitor-mediated Eg5 acetylation also causes mitotic arrest PMID 28392145. Next lab step proposed — γ-tubulin co-stain for monopolar rosette vs bundled bipolar spindles — remains appropriate to definitively separate Eg5 from stabilizer.

reflection.text: We got this right with appropriately modest confidence (p=0.64) and the final call matched unblinding: AZ-C truth = Eg5 inhibitors. Reflection by evidence:
what_was_right: Core phenotype was antimitotic with increased tubulin signal and abnormal nuclei from the lowest sampled dose: e3 at 0.03 uM already showed nuc_dna_integrated z=+19.8, tub_std z=+19.4, nuc_solidity z=-19.1; e2 at 1 uM showed tub_glcm_contrast z=+40.2, tub_mean z=+28.5, nuc_solidity z=-28.3; e10 (0.1 uM) and e11 (0.3 uM) replicated this with tub_std/tub_mean z ~+17 to +19.7 and nuc_solidity z -15.6 to -21.0. Consistency across 4 wells/doses pointed to a mitotic spindle target, not DNA damage/actin/cholesterol etc., which we correctly down-weighted in e17.

Atlas comparison shift was informative, not ignored: e4 over 2 wells was split - NSC 1/2 Microtubule stabilizers, k-neighbours 6/10 stabilizers, 4/10 Eg5 inhibitors. After adding intermediate doses e10/e11, e12 over 4 wells became NSC 3/4 Eg5 inhibitors, k-neighbours 5/10 Eg5 inhibitors, 1/10 stabilizers. We let the 4-well vote override the early 2-well vote, which was the key to getting to Eg5 vs stabilizer.

Dose trends correctly ruled down Aurora kinase inhibitors: e13 tub_mean rho=+1.00 p=0 with 4 doses shows monotonic tubulin increase consistent with antimitotic but not discriminative alone between Eg5 and stabilizer; e15 nuc_area rho=-1.00 p=0 decreasing with dose and e14 frac_large_nucleus rho=-0.20 p=0.8 no increase contradicts the large/polyploid nucleus expectation for Aurora. We therefore set Aurora to 0.05 in e17, supported by e5 microscopist listing Aurora as candidate but density lower vs DMSO not enlarged nuclei.
Cell count trend e16 rho=-0.40 p=0.6 was non-significant, so we did not over-call toxicity or proliferation block quantitatively; we treated lower density in e5 qualitatively.

Unblinding check e19 correctly showed AZ-C has no PubChem CID/ChEMBL mechanism in BBBC021 - internal code - so we did not force a structure-based prior. Post-unblinding literature check e20 'Eg5 kinesin inhibitor monopolar spindle mitotic arrest' 17 hits, 5 returned is consistent with Eg5 inhibition causing mitotic arrest and monopolar spindle formation as described in PMID 19351824, PMID 31679979 and PMID 28392145. e21 stabilizer taxol literature query 0 hits did not provide counter-support for stabilizer, and e22 taxol lookup CID 36314 was only a name-only Tubulin inhibitor control.
what_was_wrong: e2 alone was misleading if taken in isolation: tub_glcm_contrast +40.2 extreme texture plus tub_mean +28.5 can be read as microtubule stabilizer bundling, and e4 k-neighbour 6/10 stabilizers reinforced that. We did not make a premature stabilizer call but e17 kept stabilizer at 0.28 for this reason, and e5 microscopist also listed Microtubule stabilizers, Aurora, Eg5 - i.e. phenotype description with 4 fields did not resolve monopolar rosette vs bundle.

e6-e9 correctly errored 'Need at least 3 wells over 2 concentrations' with only 2 wells, but that meant initial acquisition of 1 uM + 0.03 uM (e2,e3) was insufficient to compute dose trends. Spending budget on two distant doses before atlas check delayed discrimination.

e11 0.3 uM showed tub_std +19.0 > tub_mean +17.9 similar to e3/e10 pattern, but nuc_solidity -15.6 was least negative; without image-level centrosome co-stain we could not visually confirm monopolar vs bipolar spindle, which is why next_experiment_if_real_lab proposed gamma-tubulin and pH3 flow was needed.

e12 Protein synthesis 3/10 k-neighbours was a distracting confounder that could have supported a false alternative; we correctly kept Protein synthesis at 0.0025 in e17 rather than inflating it, but it shows atlas texture features overlap non-mitotic classes.

citations.claim: K858 novel inhibitor of mitotic kinesin Eg5 induces cell death supports Eg5 inhibition linked to mitotic arrest phenotype we observed
monopolar spindle formation as Eg5-linked phenotype class described for compounds like Pyrenocine A, same class as our Eg5 call
Eg5/KIF11 acetylation mediates mitotic arrest supporting Eg5 as mitotic target

## Reflection

- Unblinding check e19 correctly showed AZ-C has no PubChem CID/ChEMBL mechanism in BBBC021 - internal code - so we did not force a structure-based prior. - e2 alone was misleading if taken in isolation: tub_glcm_contrast +40.2 extreme texture plus tub_mean +28.5 can be read as microtubule stabilizer bundling, and e4 k-neighbour 6/10 stabilizers reinforced that.
